events.title: Autumn harvest sweeps Story and Boone counties, Iowa
events.summary: The radar saw a sharp, lasting drop in the signal from standing crops across about 1,733 square kilometres of mostly farmland, the pattern expected when fields are harvested. The change first appeared on 6 September 2026 and was still spreading at the latest pass on 24 October 2026, its largest extent so far. The detection is very confident (95%), and the satellite passes every 12 days.

The detection is very confident, matching the clear drop in signal expected when standing crops are cleared from fields.

events.title: Possible flooding on farmland in Story and Boone counties, Iowa
events.summary: The satellite saw an area of mostly cropland in Story and Boone counties darken in a way that usually means smooth standing water, first on October 12, 2026, growing to about 5 square kilometers by October 24. The satellite passes every 12 days, so the next look should show whether the water is spreading or receding.
